subject.title: Bug: preflight (budget-triggered) compaction hard-capped at ~60s, ignores compaction.timeoutSeconds

question: Should the remaining fix use the open PR's filtered preflight cancellation signal, or require a config opt-out or different cancellation contract before landing?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the permanent contract determines whether lifecycle timeout aborts are ignored only for required preflight compaction and whether an additional preflight opt-out belongs in core config.

options.title: Land filtered preflight signal
options.body: Review and land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95590 if its proof and tests are acceptable, because it targets the wrong abort boundary without adding new config surface.

options.title: Require config opt-out too
options.body: Keep the abort-signal fix but also ask for a separate additive preflight disable knob if maintainers want an operator escape hatch for slow backends.

options.title: Defer for broader compaction redesign
options.body: Leave this issue open behind the broader compaction timeout work if maintainers want partial-progress and preflight cancellation solved together.

recommendation.title: Land filtered preflight signal
recommendation.body: Review and land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95590 if its proof and tests are acceptable, because it targets the wrong abort boundary without adding new config surface.

likelyOwner.reason: The history points to Vincent Koc as the strongest current owner for the auto-reply preflight compaction path and release-adjacent changes.
